Article Title: 'This is Rahul Gandhi's Mohabbat Ki Dukan': BJP on Congress leaders' Sajjan Kumar tributes
Article Text:
Sajjan Kumar was sevring life imprisonment in Delhi's Tihar Jail

NEW DELHI: The BJP on Friday hit back at the Congress after several of its leaders paid tribute to former party leader Sajjan Kumar, a convict in a 1984 anti-Sikh riots case, who died at 80 Congress MP Deepender Hooda described the death of Kumar, a former three-term Lok Sabha MP, as an "irreparable loss.""Today, the country's political landscape has suffered an irreparable loss... Sajjan Kumar ji was a leader whose connection with people in Delhi and across north India was cited as a model across the country," he said.Reacting to Hooda's remarks, BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari accused the Congress of "eulogising the killers of the Sikh community", referring to Kumar's role in the anti-Sikh riots."Congress calls late Sajjan Kumar, a man convicted in a 1984 anti-Sikh riots case, a 'role model'! How can Congress eulogise the killers of our Sikh community?" Bhandari posted on X."This is the real mindset of 'Mohabbat Ki Dukkan' (shop of love) of Rahul Gandhi and exposes the innate hate Congress has for the Sikh community!" Bhandari added, referring to a phrase used by Congress leader and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha.The BJP spokesperson further demanded that Congress apologise for "insulting" the victims of the anti-Sikh riots and "rubbing" salt into the wounds of the survivors and victims' families.Congress leader Udit Raj also described Kumar's death as a "great loss" for the party."It is a great loss for the Congress. He was a very senior Congress leader, and it will be difficult to fill the void... He did a lot of work, especially for the poor," Raj stated.Sajjan Kumar died at Delhi's Safdarjung Hospital on Thursday."Sajjan Kumar was brought to Safdarjung Hospital by police with altered sensorium around 11 am. He was immediately admitted and resuscitation measures were initiated. Despite providing all necessary medical and life-support measures, he could not be saved and passed away at 12:30 pm," the hospital's statement read."He was a known case of high blood pressure and Parkinson's disease and had a history of multiple hospital admissions in the past," the statement added.Kumar was serving multiple life sentences after his conviction in cases linked to the 1984 anti-Sikh riots in Delhi.He was sentenced to life imprisonment by the Delhi High Court on December 17, 2018, in a case related to the killing of five Sikhs and the burning of a gurdwara during the anti-Sikh riots.He was also sentenced to life imprisonment by a Delhi court in February 2025 in another case relating to the killing of two Sikh men during the riots.Kumar resigned from the primary membership of the Congress after the 2018 conviction.
Article Summary: Congress MP Deepender Hooda described the death of Kumar as an "irreparable loss" BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari accused the Congress of "eulogising the killers of the Sikh community" Kumar was serving multiple life sentences after his conviction in cases linked to the 1984 anti-Sikh riots in Delhi.

Article Title: SC: Can't assume Speaker's role to direct MLAs' disqualification
Article Text:

New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Wednesday disagreed with the contention of Shiv Sena (UBT) that it should disqualify the MLAs who have crossed over to the rival faction led by Eknath Shinde , saying that it cannot assume Speaker's role and decide disqualification petitions against MLAs.A bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was hearing pleas filed by Sena (UBT) challenging the Speaker's call rejecting its pleas for disqualification of rebel MLAs led by Eknath Shinde and EC's decision to recognise Sena (Shinde) as the original party to allot them the bow and arrow symbol.While hearing petitions filed by Sena UBT, the SC said it can at best set aside an erroneous order of House’s presiding officer and direct him to adjudicate the plea for disqualification afresh in conformity with guidelines laid down for the purpose.Shiv Sena split in June 2022 bringing down the MVA govt headed by Uddhav Thackeray. The rebel MLAs went on to support BJP-led NDA to form the govt in Maharashtra with Shinde as CM. Assembly elections were held in Nov 2024, wherein the BJP-led NDA secured a thumping majority.“We cannot assume the speaker’s role and decide the disqualification petitions ourselves. We can’t issue a mandamus that the MLAs, in the facts of the matter, stood disqualified.At best, we can set aside the speaker’s order and ask him to decide afresh in sync with parameters of the Tenth Schedule,” said Justice Bagchi.Senior advocate Devadatt Kamat argued that the speaker erred by not disqualifying Shinde-led rebel MLAs as the anti-defection law permits split only in a political party and not one in legislature party.He said that since there was no adjudication of a split in the political party led by Thackeray, the rebel legislators cannot be saved from the disqualification.“Shiv Sena of Thackerays has been using the bow and arrow symbol for decades and the Shinde faction cannot steal it through illegitimate means,” said senior advocate Kapil Sibal and requested the court to freeze the symbol.He added that the party belongs to the Thackerays and the Shinde-faction cannot claim to be the original party as they are defectors who have sinned under the Tenth Schedule.Kamat will conclude his arguments Thursday, which would be followed by Shinde faction lawyers presenting their side of arguments.
Article Summary: Shiv Sena split in June 2022 bringing down the MVA govt headed by Uddhav Thackeray. The rebel MLAs went on to support BJP-led NDA to form the govt in Maharashtra with Shinde as CM.

Article Title: Ugc Net: Will hold retest of 3 subjects of UGC-NET: Govt
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Centre informed Delhi high court Wednesday that a retest is being conducted for three subjects of UGC-NET June-2026 examination, including Sociology, following complaints of errors in the question papers.Taking note of the submission by solicitor general Tushar Mehta, Justice Jasmeet Singh disposed of a plea filed by a candidate who appeared for the Sociology exam, which sought a stay on the declaration of results pending an independent probe and re-conduct of the exam following allegations of paper leak and errors in the question paper.While English and Commerce papers will be held on Sept 9, the Sociology paper will be held on Sept 10, Mehta told Delhi HC, adding that the decision addresses the student's grievance.In a public notice, NTA had acknowledged that it received several complaints about multiple errors in the question papers of three subjects and formed a committee to look into the matter. Article Title: Who was Sajjan Kumar? From 3-time Congress MP to 1984 riots convict
Article Text:
Former Congress MP Sajjan Kumar has died, Safdarjung Hospital authorities confirmed.

Who was Sajjan Kumar

NEW DELHI: Former Congress leader and 1984 anti-Sikh riots convict Sajjan Kumar died in Tihar jail on Thursday at the age of 80.Kumar was brought dead to Delhi's Safdarjung Hospital, news agency ANI reported, citing sources.The three-time parliamentarian was serving a life sentence in connection with the 1984 Sikh riots that followed the assassination of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.Kumar began his political career as a municipal councillor from Delhi's Nangloi in 1977. At the time, he was also the general secretary of the Pradesh Congress Committee.He was among the close allies of Indira Gandhi's younger son, Sanjay Gandhi.Kumar rose through the political ranks and won the Outer Delhi Lok Sabha seat in the 1980 elections. He defeated Chaudhary Brahm Prakash, Delhi's first chief minister.However, the aftermath of the 1984 riots brought his political career to a halt after he was accused of being criminally responsible for the violence.He withdrew from public glare and continued contributing to the party from behind the scenes.After a long gap, he returned to active politics, winning re-election to the Lok Sabha for a second term in 1991, and again in 2004.For more than three decades, Kumar faced several criminal cases linked to the violence. The cases saw different outcomes, including acquittals and convictions by various courts.In the Delhi Raj Nagar case, involving the killing of five members of a family and the burning of a gurudwara, the Delhi high court overturned a trial court's acquittal on December 17, 2018. It convicted Kumar and sentenced him to life imprisonment.Kumar surrendered and had been in jail since December 2018 after resigning from the primary membership of the party.In the Saraswati Vihar murder case, involving the killing of Jaswant Singh and his son Tarundeep Singh on November 1, 1984, a trial court had earlier acquitted Kumar. On February 25, 2025, Special Judge Kaveri Baweja sentenced him to a second life term.The court spared him the death penalty, citing his old age, ailments and conduct while serving his earlier life sentence.In the Janakpuri and Vikaspuri violence case, a Rouse Avenue court acquitted Kumar on January 22 of charges related to the killing of Sohan Singh and his son-in-law Avtar Singh, and the burning of Gurcharan Singh.On May 26, the Delhi high court issued notice on an appeal against the acquittal of former MP Sajjan Kumar in the 1984 anti-Sikh riots case.Kumar had repeatedly sought bail and relief on medical grounds during his imprisonment.
Article Summary: Former Congress leader and 1984 anti-Sikh riots convict Sajjan Kumar died in Tihar jail on Thursday at the age of 80. Kumar was brought dead to Delhi's Safdarjung Hospital, news agency ANI reported, citing sources. The three-time parliamentarian was serving a life sentence in connection with the 1984 Sikh riots.

Article Title: Telangana tantrik held in Latur occult ritual case involving minor girl
Article Text:
The occultists is the 14th person arrested in the case

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





A 38-year-old tantrik (occultist) from Telangana , allegedly tasked with performing a black magic ritual to make Rs 15-20 crore “rain” from the sky, was arrested on Thursday. The arrest came four days after Udgir Rural police foiled the alleged ritual, which involved a 15-year-old girl brought from Andhra Pradesh Police identified the accused as Balaji Mangal Balraj of Chinar Kodmangal village in Telangana’s Kamareddy district. “He was arrested from Telangana,” Latur superintendent of police Amol Tambe said. Balraj is the 14th person arrested in the case.The case came to light around 2am on Aug 16 near Karadkhel Pati on the Latur-Udgir road, about 20km from Udgir, when police rescued the minor girl and prevented the alleged ritual from being carried out after receiving on a tip-off. Police had earlier arrested 13 accused from the spot, while one suspect escaped. Another accused, a Pune resident who was allegedly slated to perform part of the ritual, did not arrive after learning about the possibility of a police raid.Investigators are now probing an alleged interstate network behind the ritual. The 15 accused named in the case are from Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka.The 13 accused arrested earlier remain in police custody and are being questioned about the alleged conspiracy, individual roles and the circumstances under which the minor was brought to the site.Police are also examining whether the girl was specifically brought for the ritual and whether others helped.A case has been registered at Udgir Rural police station under Section 3 (3) of the Maharashtra Prevention and Eradication of Human Sacrifice and other Inhuman, Evil and Aghori Practices and Black Magic Act, along with sections 12 and 18 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (Pocso) Act. Inspector Dilip Gade is leading the investigation.
Article Summary: A 38-year-old tantrik from Telangana, allegedly tasked with performing a black magic ritual to make Rs 15-20 crore “rain” from the sky, was arrested on Thursday. The arrest came four days after Udgir Rural police foiled the alleged ritual. The 15 accused named in the case are from Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka.

Article Title: Jewellery, cash worth Rs8.6L stolen from house in Kolhapur
Article Text:
Kolhapur

:





Gold and silver jewellery along with cash, collectively worth around Rs 8.6 lakh, were stolen from a house in Tarabai Park area of Kolhapur city on Monday between 5.30am and 7.30am.According to the police, the burglars broke open the rear door of the house located in Sahajivan Parisar area by using a metal rod. After gaining access they found the keys of the cupboard locker in which jewelry and cash were kept.A complaint has been filed at Shahupuri police station by the owner of the house Shirish Sadashiv Sankpal (31). The police have registered the case under sections 305(A) (theft) , 331(3) (trespass) and 331(4) of BNS 2023 on Wednesday.“The burglars must have studied the area and residents of the house before executing the crime. They also knew where the keys of the locker were kept,” a police officer said.Later on Wednesday, the police arrested a Kadamwadi resident, 42-year-old Sachin Sadashiv Hasurkar, and recovered the valuables stolen from Sankpal’s house.
Article Summary: Gold and silver jewellery along with cash, collectively worth around Rs 8.6 lakh, were stolen from a house in Tarabai Park area of Kolhapur city. The burglars broke open the rear door of the house located in Sahajivan Parisar area by using a metal rod.

Article Title: Ambernath BJP-MNS clash: Case registered against 2 BJP corporators, five others
Article Text:
A new case was filed against seven individuals, including two BJP corporators, following a clash.





AMBERNATH: The political clash between BJP and Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) workers in Ambernath has taken a fresh turn, with Shivaji Nagar police registering a fresh case against seven people, including two BJP corporators, on the complaint of an MNS worker who was injured in the incident.The latest case was registered on Sunday on the complaint of Suhas Ghag, a relative of MNS Ambernath city chief Shailesh Shirke, who was also injured in the clash. Police have booked BJP corporators Abhijit Karanjule and Pawan Walekar along with five others under sections 118(1), 115(2), 189(2), 190, 191(2) and 324(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).The development comes days after police arrested Shirke and some of his associates for allegedly assaulting BJP office-bearer Laxmi Narayan Chauhan at his office in Vadavali.A subsequent clash between BJP and MNS workers at Shivaji Nagar police station further escalated tensions.MNS leaders had alleged that police took one-sided action by arresting their office-bearers while failing to act against BJP workers allegedly involved in the assault on Shirke. MNS leader Avinash Jadhav had demanded action against those responsible.Following the demand, MNS district president Bandu Deshmukh had announced a protest on Sunday against what the party termed one-sided police action. However, after police registered an FIR against BJP workers, MNS withdrew its protest.
Article Summary: A new case was filed against seven individuals, including two BJP corporators, following a clash. The latest case was registered on the complaint of Suhas Ghag, a relative of MNS Ambernath city chief Shailesh Shirke, who was also injured in the clash.

Article Title: Rs 67 lakh job fraud on promise of Pune civic body jobs
Article Text:
Representative image

Pune:





Four persons were booked for allegedly duping six aspirants of Rs67 lakh in exchange for securing them jobs with Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC).A 22-year-old man from Nandoshi village in the Khadakwasla area lodged a complaint with Sinhagad Road police. Based on his complaint, a case has been registered against the four accused under Sections 316 (criminal breach of trust), 318 (cheating), 337 (forgery), 338 (forgery of valuable security), and 340 (forged document or electronic record and using it as genuine) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).A police officer said, “The suspect had approached the complainant around two years ago and promised to secure him a job with the PMC as a peon, supervisor or security personnel. They allegedly collected Rs67 lakh from the complainant and other five job aspirants between 2024 and June 2026, assuring them of jobs with the civic body.”Allegedly, the suspects also gave the aspirants joining letters and identity cards bearing fake stamps of PMC officials. When the complainant and others approached PMC, they found the documents were fake. “When the complainant questioned them, they avoided him and gave him evasive replies. Realising they had been cheated, the complainant and others approached the police. Our investigation is underway,” the officer added.
Article Summary: A 22-year-old man from Nandoshi village in the Khadakwasla area lodged a complaint with Sinhagad Road police. A case has been registered against the four accused under Sections 316 (criminal breach of trust), 318 (cheating), 337 (forgery) and 340 (forged document or electronic record)

Article Title: Night patrol under lens as goons target rly passengers
Article Text:
rly

Nagpur:





Four miscreants waylaid a native of Madhya Pradesh on Ram Jhula and beat him with a baton while he was heading to Nagpur railway station on early Tuesday. The incident is the latest in a series of attacks on railway passengers heading to the station in the early hours.The area in and around Ram Jhula has a history of such crimes. There is no CCTV coverage and police post that once stood there has been dismantled. With almost zero police presence in the night, knife-wielding goons are targeting passengers in and around the station, with two murders and numerous robberies in the last one year.Complaints have been lodged at Ganeshpeth and Sitabuldi police stations about commuters being robbed and assaulted by in areas near the railway station.In the latest incident, Arvind Prajapati, 33-year-old farmer from Kolar Tola in Silwani tehsil of Raisen district in MP, was walking towards the railway station around 3.30am. Two miscreants grabbed his hands and feet while another snatched ₹5,650 in cash and a cellphone, valued at ₹15,000, from his trouser pocket. One the miscreants then assaulted him with a baton and threatened to kill him if he approached police.Prajapati lodged a complaint at Ganeshpeth police station. No arrests have been made so far. Police teams are examining CCTV footage from the area.In a recent case, a carpenter from Jharkhand was robbed of ₹30,000 at knifepoint near Empress Mall Gate while travelling in an e-rickshaw to catch a train. Three men intercepted and threatened him, and fled on a two-wheeler after snatching cash from the carpenter.Earlier, a couple was harassed and then attacked with knife by three miscreants on Ganesh Tekdi road while trying to reach the station. A few days ago, three persons robbed a passenger in an autorickshaw en route to the railway station.Complaints were filed at Ganeshpeth and Sitabuldi police stations where cases have been registered under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, but the accused remain at large. The pattern of violence against late-night and early-morning travellers has raised serious questions about the effectiveness of night patrolling in Nagpur.
Article Summary: Four miscreants waylaid a native of Madhya Pradesh on Ram Jhula and beat him with a baton. The incident is the latest in a series of attacks on railway passengers heading to the station in the early hours. With almost zero police presence in the night, knife-wielding goons are targeting passengers in and around the station.

Article Title: Nashik police bust sex racket, one woman rescued
Article Text:
Nashik:





The central crime branch of Nashik city police busted a sex racket that was operating under the guise of a fitness centre in the Mumbai Naka area.The raid was carried out by the anti-human trafficking unit (AHTU) on Wednesday, leading to the rescue of one woman.Acting on confidential information, officials learnt that illegal commercial sex activities were being carried out at a bungalow in an area under Mumbai Naka.The establishment was masquerading as an operational fitness centre. Upon verifying the information, the police raided the bungalow and confirmed the illicit operations.Following the raid, the Mumbai Naka police registered a case under sections of the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act against two individuals, and rescued a woman who was pressed into prostitution by the two persons for their own benefit.The raid was executed under the directions of the Nashik city police Commissioner Sandeep Karnik, DCP (Crime) Kirankumar Chavan, and ACP (Crime) Sandeep Mitke. Senior police inspector Yogesh Deshmukh led the operation raid.
Article Summary: The central crime branch of Nashik city police busted a sex racket that was operating under the guise of a fitness centre in the Mumbai Naka area. The raid was carried out by the anti-human trafficking unit (AHTU) on Wednesday, leading to the rescue of one woman.

Article Title: ‘Anti-national decision’: Amit Shah slams Congress over Vande Mataram row
Article Text:
Called the move 'anti-national'

Chennai:





Union home minister Amit Shah on Thursday launched a direct attack on Congress , labelling its decision to restrict the singing of Vande Mataram to just two stanzas as “anti-national.”Responding to Congress Working Committee’s resolution on the national song, Shah accused the party of reviving its decades-old “politics of appeasement.” Shah was speaking to ANI news agency on the sidelines of the South Zone Chief Ministers’ Conference in Mamallapuram.He alleged that Congress split Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay’s national song in 1937 for Muslim appeasement, effectively laying the groundwork for India’s partition.Shah contrasted the opposition’s stance with that of the Narendra Modi govt, highlighting that the ruling dispensation had legally framed and restored the full version of Vande Mataram to strengthen national unity.Targeting the opposition leadership, Shah expressed surprise over Rahul Gandhi driving this revival of appeasement politics. Shah warned that the country had already paid a heavy historical price for dividing the national song and called on the nation to unite against the decision, asserting that the BJP strongly condemned the move.
Article Summary: Amit Shah accused the party of reviving its decades-old “politics of appeasement” He alleged that Congress split Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay’s national song in 1937 for Muslimappeasement. Shah warned that the country had already paid a heavy historical price.

Article Title: Lady doctor arrested near Salem for illegal fetal gender determination
Article Text: SALEM: Police on Wednesday arrested a lady doctor in Vazhapadi in Salem district on charges of illegally determining and disclosing the gender of fetuses to pregnant women. Health department officials seized scan equipment, abortion pills and cash from a clinic the doctor, Selvamba Rajkumar, was running in the area. They sealed the clinic.Authorities said the clinic on the Cuddalore Road charged pregnant women additional fees to reveal the gender of the unborn child.Acting on a complaint, a team led by joint director Dr S P Nandhini, Attur district health officer Dr N Yoganand and Vazhapadi Government Hospital chief medical officer Dr Ramesh Kumar raided the facility.They found that Dr Selvamba Rajkumar had received Rs 30,000 from a pregnant woman to determine the gender of her fetus. Dr Nandini said the doctor had been handed over to police for legal proceedings.Health department officials said this was not the first violation by the clinic. It had been raided twice earlier, and Dr Selvamba Rajkumar had faced restrictions on conducting scans and treatments, they said. Cases were registered against her then too.
Article Summary: Health department officials seized scan equipment, abortion pills and cash from a clinic the doctor, Selvamba Rajkumar, was running. Authorities said the clinic on the Cuddalore Road charged pregnant women additional fees to reveal the gender of the unborn child. Dr Nandini said the doctor had been handed over to police for legal proceedings.

Article Title: Kerala makeup artist arrested for allegedly insulting PM Narendra Modi
Article Text:
Transgender influencer Jaanmoni Das was arrested by Kozhikode cyber police for alleged remarks on PM Narendra Modi.





KOZHIKODE: Transgender makeup artist and social media influencer Jaanmoni Das was arrested by the Kozhikode City cyber police for alleged derogatory remarks on PM Narendra Modi on social media.Abin K R, of Thiruvambady in Kozhikode and the owner of the social media channel MollywoodConnect - which had posted the video featuring Das - and Sajith K S of Karimba in Palakkad, who shot and uploaded the video, were also arrested.All three were released on station bail on completion of legal formalities.The mobile phone used by MollywoodConnect to shoot the video was seized from Sajith, who is also the channel's cameraman, for further examination.Kozhikode City cyber police had registered a case against Jaanmoni based on a complaint by Mahila Morcha state president Navya Haridas. Jaanmoni made the remarks on recent Jantar Mantar protests.Mahila Morcha and the BJP had alleged that Jaanmoni's remarks not only insulted the prime minister, but she also made derogatory comments about his parents. Following intense protests organised by Mahila Morcha, Jaanmoni issued an apology on her social media page. She stated that language limitations led to the remarks and that she did not intend to cause offence. She requested forgiveness.She was summoned by police via a notice and her arrest was recorded on Wednesday and was subsequently released on bail.
Article Summary: Jaanmoni Das was arrested by the Kozhikode City cyber police for alleged derogatory remarks on PM Narendra Modi on social media. Owner of the social media channel MollywoodConnect and Sajith K S of Karimba in Palakkad, who shot and uploaded the video, were also arrested. All three were released on station bail.

Article Title: Man wanted in assault case arrested after 37 years
Article Text:
Idukki

:





A 61-year-old man who had been absconding for 37 years in connection with an assault case was arrested from Karnataka on Tuesday. The arrested person is Thomas alias Titi of Kalkoonthal village.According to the police, Thomas allegedly attacked and injured a neighbour with a stone at Irattyar North in 1989.Kattappana Police recently received information that he was staying in Siddapur in Karnataka’s Kodagu district. Acting on the information, a team from the district police chief’s fugitive-tracing squad, along with civil police officer Saju Raj, arrested him.Thomas was brought to Kattappana and was produced before a court on Thursday. He was remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: A 61-year-old man had been absconding for 37 years in connection with an assault case. The arrested person is Thomas alias Titi of Kalkoonthal village. Thomas allegedly attacked and injured a neighbour with a stone at Irattyar North in 1989.

Article Title: DGP’s foreign visit: No probe needed for now, Kerala HC told
Article Text:
ADGP S Sreejith

Kochi

:





Additional chief secretary of the home department Minhaj Alam on Thursday informed the high court that no vigilance inquiry was warranted, for the time being, against DGP S Sreejith on a complaint alleging that he had attended the inauguration of a private enterprise abroad while wearing his police uniform.Alam made the submission when he appeared before the court in compliance with its direction for his personal appearance over the non-compliance with an earlier directive in the matter. The case arose from a petition filed by Dipin Edavana, an assistant motor vehicle inspector from Kannur, seeking a vigilance inquiry into the allegation.The HC had earlier directed the vigilance department to consider the complaint. Subsequently, Alam directed Dipin to appear for a hearing on April 20. Dipin did not attend, contending that the hearing was proposed to be held jointly in the presence of Sreejith. Thereafter, a report was submitted stating that Dipin had failed to cooperate with the inquiry and had raised baseless allegations without bona fides. The court set aside the report and directed Alam to reconsider the complaint after granting Dipin a personal hearing and pass fresh orders within three weeks.When the directive was not complied with and Alam sought additional time, the court directed his personal appearance.Appearing on Thursday, Alam submitted that the directive had since been complied with and that an order had been issued stating that a vigilance investigation was not warranted for the time being. The court orally criticised him for having his subordinate file the application seeking additional time instead of filing it himself. However, the court closed the petition after recording Alam’s submission, while preserving Dipin’s liberty to pursue further remedies in accordance with law.Meanwhile, the bench dispensed with Alam’s personal appearance on Friday in another contempt case alleging non-compliance with the court’s directive to consider the promotion of P Sreekumar, a police inspector who had been arrayed as an accused in two cases in connection with the Monson Mavunkal case. Following Alam’s submission that Sreekumar’s promotion would be considered at the next DPC meeting, the court directed him to file an affidavit to that effect and dispensed with his personal appearance.
Article Summary: Alam made the submission when he appeared before the court in compliance with its direction for his personal appearance. The case arose from a petition filed by Dipin Edavana, an assistant motor vehicle inspector from Kannur, seeking a vigilance inquiry into the allegation.

Article Title: Muttil tree felling: Kerala HC junks Roji Augustine’s plea for stay in trial
Article Text:
Kerala high court

Kochi:





The high court on Thursday dismissed a petition filed by Roji Augustine, the prime accused in the Muttil mass tree-felling cases in Wayanad, seeking a stay of the ongoing trial in a related cheating case before the Chottanikkara magistrate court, and directed him to approach the trial court for relief.The case pending before the Chottanikkara court against the petitioner was that he, along with his brothers, Anto and Jose Kutty, had allegedly cheated M M Aliyar of Karimukal in Ernakulam by selling him timber allegedly felled and transported illegally from the area under the Meppadi forest range in Wayanad district. Aliyar was allegedly made to believe that the timber was accompanied by the requisite passes issued by the forest department.According to the petitioner, the case registered by the Meppadi range forest officer against them for the illegal mass felling of trees in South Muttil in the Meppadi forest range of Wayanad district had not yet been concluded. The present cheating case arose from the same incident. Accordingly, the petitioner sought a stay of further trial proceedings in the case before the Chottanikkara magistrate court until the investigation was completed.However, the bench of Justice C S Dias, while considering the petition, noted that the petitioner had not approached the trial court for the relief sought and had instead approached the HC directly. The bench held that the petition was not maintainable and dismissed it, directing the petitioner to approach the trial court for the relief.
Article Summary: The high court dismissed a petition filed by Roji Augustine, the prime accused in the Muttil mass tree-felling cases in Wayanad. Augustine was seeking a stay of the ongoing trial in a related cheating case before the Chottanikkara magistrate court. The case pending against the petitioner was that he had allegedly cheated M M Aliyar.
